summary: Jok Prince is a long-running Bang Rak shop known for Cantonese-style Thai rice porridge with a smoky aroma. Choose pork balls and optional offal, soft-boiled or century egg; fried dough is a classic side. It is a simple, inexpensive meal stop rather than a destination for elaborate service or a long sit-down.
whyGo: Try jok, a very soft rice porridge with a distinctive smoke note and a choice of pork and egg toppings.
The small shop offers a direct look at an established Bangkok neighborhood food business on Charoen Krung Road.
bestFor: An early breakfast or casual second meal in Bang Rak.
Travelers curious about Thai-Chinese comfort food and organ-meat options.
skipIf: You need confirmed step-free access, roomy seating, or a quiet dining room; reliable accessibility details are not published.
You avoid pork, offal, or busy, informal eateries.
duration: Allow about 30–60 minutes including a possible queue; this is a planning estimate, and the compact shop may turn tables quickly.
cost: Budget roughly ฿50–150 per person as a planning estimate, depending on toppings, sides and drinks. Time Out listed a basic bowl at ฿40 and patongo at ฿20 in September 2024; prices may have changed by December 2026.
hours: The Tourism Authority of Thailand's Japanese site lists 06:00–12:00 and 16:30–22:00, with service ending when porridge runs out. Time Out lists 06:00–13:00 and 15:00–23:00. Hours conflict, so verify close to your visit; arrive early for the widest topping choice.
bestTime: Go early in the morning, ideally before 08:00, for breakfast and the best chance of finding the full topping selection. The evening session is an alternative if the morning does not fit.
gettingThere: At 1391 Charoen Krung Road in Bang Rak, near the former Prince cinema. OpenRice describes it as about a 10-minute walk from Saphan Taksin BTS Exit 3; allow for Bangkok heat and traffic, or use a taxi/ride-hail for the last leg.
booking: No booking method is listed by the tourism authority or Time Out. Treat it as walk-in, and call +66 89 795 2629 to check opening or stock before making a special trip.
accessibility: No dependable published information on step-free entry, accessible toilets or seating space was found. The shop is described as small and informal; contact the venue about specific access needs before visiting.
practicalTips: Order the pork-ball jok first; add soft-boiled egg or century egg, and try patongo (fried dough) if you want a side.
Time Out reports that some toppings may sell out later in the morning; arrive before 08:00 if selection matters.
The displayed menu and staff may not support detailed English conversation; a saved photo of your preferred topping can help.
Keep a little cash available. Payment methods are not consistently confirmed in the sources reviewed.
decemberNotes: December is generally a popular, comparatively less rainy time to explore Bangkok, but the restaurant has no published December 2026 holiday schedule. Check opening hours and call ahead around public holidays; do not assume normal split-shift service or that the pot will last until closing.
uncertainties: Published opening hours differ between the Tourism Authority of Thailand and Time Out; confirm directly before travel.
The latest sourced menu prices are from 2024 and should be treated as a guide, not a December 2026 quote.
Accessibility, payment methods, current booking policy and holiday closures are not confirmed.
